answer: The protocol mandates 5,000 megabytes of memory-hard work to gate each identity, treating every agent as a prism that refracts tasks into distinct compute streams. A verifier enforces this by sampling random memory offsets, ensuring that no two agents occupy the same karst-like geologic formation of data. Each identity must maintain an isolated heap within its own garden of RAM, where collisions trigger a permanent lockout. An honest participant pays for one unit of compute, whereas 1,000 fake identities incur 1,000 times that cost, as each requires a unique, non-pooled memory enclave.
